provenance.method: Practical disruption-planning route added across mobility/sensory/communication needs without guaranteeing operator support.

question: Changes, delays and platform or stop changes make travel hard. What can I check before a journey?
why_it_matters: Predictability, communication and contingency planning can matter as much as physical access for some neurodivergent and disabled travellers.
current_understanding: Before travel, inspect current operator/station accessibility information, assistance/contact routes, interchange details and disruption channels. Where possible, identify a fallback or place to ask for help. ND Oracle cannot guarantee a journey will run as planned or that every announced accessibility feature will be available.
evidence_needed: More operator-published non-phone contact, sensory/cognitive information and disruption accessibility metadata.
reopening_conditions: Operators publish stable structured accessibility/disruption metadata that supports a richer governed comparison.
dissent: More planning can reduce uncertainty for some people but increase cognitive load for others; the route should support choice rather than prescribe a single strategy.
